text.text: WEST WING | AN ISLAND THAT TURNED ITS BACK ON THE SEA
Seawalls ring Malé, with only two soft edges left to the water. The West wing reopens one of them as the Ocean Hub: a beach, diving and swimming.
Taller homes lifted on green bases, cut open with courtyards for cross-ventilation, with one plot left free as open space. The North wing’s capstone plots follow the new guidelines.
The parti in four steps, one for each wing of Fahi-Malé.
EAST WING | THE HUB OF THE ATOLLS
Every island connects through Malé. The East wing turns that traffic into a proper arrival: one terminal for ferries, airport boats and bridge buses.
Old Malé was low homes set in walled compounds, with shade, trees and air inside every plot. The South wing brings that back through breeze cuts, superblocks and pocket parks.
